title: The adhan's words
hookLine: Allah is greatest, I testify, come to prayer, come to success, then the same at the start

lines: COME TO SUCCESS, FROM A ROOFTOP.
A DRIVER, A STUDENT, A GRANDMOTHER.
cards: Come to success. Of everything a voice could shout from a rooftop at dawn, that's an odd choice. Not come to duty.
Not come, or else. Come to success, hayya ala al-falah, called out over the street at each prayer time, to anyone within earshot. A delivery driver hears it at a red light.
A student hears it through a dorm window. A grandmother hears it from a phone app in the kitchen. The whole call is a handful of short phrases.

teach.b: Year three heard the adhan sound across Africa; today, its words in order. Sunan Abu Dawud, number 499, records them as a companion, Abdullah ibn Zayd, received them. It opens: Allahu akbar, Allah is greatest.

Then the two testimonies: ashhadu an la ilaha illallah, I testify there is no god but Allah; ashhadu anna Muhammadan rasulullah, I testify that Muhammad is the messenger of Allah. Then two invitations.
Hayya ala as-salah, come to prayer. Hayya ala al-falah, come to success.

teach.h: IT CLOSES THE WAY IT BEGAN.
teach.b: And it closes the way it began: Allahu akbar, and la ilaha illallah. Notice the ring.

teach.h: THE LISTENER ANSWERS: NO POWER BUT WITH GOD.
teach.b: The call starts with God's greatness and the testimony, swings out to the listener with two invitations, and comes home to the same words.

For the dawn call, Sunan Abu Dawud, number 500, adds a line after the invitations: as-salatu khayrun min an-nawm, prayer is better than sleep. And this path has heard how Shia Muslims add their own lines.
The listener has a part, too.

teach.h: HAYYA ALA AL-FALAH. COME TO SUCCESS.
teach.b: In Sahih Muslim, number 385, the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, teaches that when you hear the call you repeat each phrase after the caller, but at come to prayer and come to success you answer la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah: there is no power and no strength except with God.
You're invited to success, and you answer that you can't get there on your own strength.
The Qur'an names the call too, in Pickthall's translation: "When the call is heard for the prayer of the day of congregation, haste unto remembrance of Allah."

how: A muezzin calls the adhan when each prayer time begins, from the mosque or over a speaker, and the hadith teaches those who hear it to repeat the phrases after him, answering the two invitations with la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah.

o: the private prayers each person whispers before praying
greatness, two testimonies, two invitations, then home again
verses of the Qur'an recited aloud from the minaret at dawn

games.q: the adhan's words — tap the pairs.

s: the adhan ends with the same words it began with
it opens and closes with Allahu akbar and the testimony, la ilaha illallah.
a listener just stays silent during the adhan
Muslim 385: repeat after the caller, and answer the invitations with no power except with God.
prayer is better than sleep is added to the dawn call
Abu Dawud 500 records the line for the dawn call.

games.q: you hear the caller say hayya ala al-falah, come to success. what does the hadith teach you to answer?
o: there is no power and no strength except with God.
say nothing until the call ends.
games.why: Muslim 385: repeat the other phrases, but answer the invitations with la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah.

practice: Say the words quietly, or just listen: Allahu akbar, ashhadu an la ilaha illallah, ashhadu anna Muhammadan rasulullah, hayya ala as-salah, hayya ala al-falah, Allahu akbar, la ilaha illallah.

Then go back to the two invitations and stay there: come to prayer, come to success. If you pray, practice the answer, la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah; if not, notice what the call names as success.

wordCard.voice: The adhan's words. Greatness, two testimonies, two invitations, and greatness and testimony again, a call shaped like a ring. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: come to success, the adhan's second invitation.

carryVoice: Your line: come to success. And the answer: not on my own strength. Tomorrow, the iqamah.

sources.q: When the call is heard for the prayer of the day of congregation, haste unto remembrance of Allah
